title: Verify useful BitTorrent-v2 blocks before a whole piece completes

definition.title: Verify useful BitTorrent-v2 blocks before a whole piece completes
definition.source_excerpt: The 579,704-byte fMP4 was hashed as BEP52-style 16-KiB leaves. The first complete init+media fragment ended at byte 91,196, requiring 6 leaves / 98,304 bytes, or 37.5% of a 256-KiB logical piece. Each required leaf was verified against the file's SHA-256 Merkle pieces root; wrong proof, wrong position, and altered-file controls were rejected. Only the verified prefix was exposed to MSE. Chromium buffered about one second and presented 13 frames before the remainder of that logical piece was available. This demonstrates earlier useful verification for a clear random-access media prefix; a full peer-protocol/hash-request implementation remains outside the pilot.
definition.impact_basis: Potentially removes substantial work from an eligible playback, seek, preparation, retention or repeated interaction. Scope comes from the cited card; exposure and effect size are unmeasured.
definition.default_next_action: Locate one real repeated read/index/validation boundary and its trusted source identity. Separate logical requests from transferred or physical-disk bytes.
definition.minimum_probe: Replay a short owned range/seek trace on a tiny indexed fixture, including its first cold operation, with the same source and authorization. Reuse the existing reader.
definition.initial_screen: Locate one real repeated read/index/validation boundary and its trusted source identity. Separate logical requests from transferred or physical-disk bytes. Replay a short owned range/seek trace on a tiny indexed fixture, including its first cold operation, with the same source and authorization. Reuse the existing reader.
definition.primary_metric: Total bytes and time to correct startup/target, including cold index/identity acquisition; bounded retained bytes.
definition.scope_contract: Source/version identity, requested exact sample/frame, dependency coverage and byte-range accounting.
definition.negative_control: Change the source/version or corrupt an offset/proof and cancel one consumer. No stale or unverified bytes may be published.
definition.stop_boundary: Do not build a generic cache, transport server or index service for a first pass. Preserve a lower-cost component decision if real integration is E3.
definition.shared_prerequisite: Authorized seekable byte provider and a known oracle for sample prerequisites; no guessed remote-source semantics.
definition.reopen_condition: A new applicable workload, resolved prerequisite, better independent oracle, or materially different bounded implementation changes the recorded decision.
definition.relevance_basis: Editorial fit to ordinary Demuxe playback goals, not measured prevalence; rerank after one local opportunity audit.

screen.basis: Actual browser verifies BEP52 SHA256 file-root proofs before exposing32768B prefix to MSE. All48 pictures match independent complete native-source oracle;11 arrive before450ms delayed remaining leaves. Wrong root/proof/position/changed bytes reject with zero unverified publication; stale tail rejects. Against cheaper complete-file tree verification baseline,11 paired fresh owners improve first correct picture by median448.56ms, above200ms gate. This qualifies the authenticated byte-provider component, not a peer protocol or production transport.

correctness.basis: Independent Python recursive root matches node-authored balanced tree and pinned bencoded metainfo. Browser WebCrypto validates five leaves, including short final and zero-hash padding. All48 source pictures and every timed presented picture exact; four hostile proof/data controls and cancelled source-generation publication reject; owners close.

performance.basis: 11 alternating pairs with first2leaves/proofs available at start and remaining3 at450ms. Candidate verifies partial leaves; cheaper baseline computes complete tree once. Includes cryptography, copies, fresh media owners, capture and teardown; common trusted-root discovery and runtime excluded. Not physical network or CPU benefit.
